caption: The video captures a single white tundra swan with a yellow-and-black bill gliding upright across calm, pale blue-grey water. Its body and long neck are mirrored in a clear reflection directly beneath, which elongates and softens as the surface ripples. Behind the bird a dark, stony shoreline slopes to the waterline, and a few strands of floating dark twigs drift past. The swan faces left and makes slow forward progress, the background debris sliding rightward relative to its upright posture while a gentle wake trails off to its right. Head and neck angle shift only marginally, the bill tilting slightly at times. The swan remains upright and afloat. The framing of the bank changes gradually, and the swan continues a slow leftward glide through rippled water.
relations: Swan's slow leftward glide causes its mirrored reflection beneath to elongate and soften as surface ripples spread.
Forward motion makes floating twigs drift rightward relative to the swan, while a gentle wake trails off to its right.
Upright posture persists; head and neck angle shift only marginally, with the bill tilting slightly during the glide.
As the swan advances, the dark stony shoreline framing shifts gradually across the background.
